results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
The deck is submitted and legal. It's a Golgari self-mill brew (B/G with a light blue splash) that uses Town Greeter and Overlord of the Balemurk to fill the graveyard, then Superior Spider-Man copies the best creature there and Bringer of the Last Gift returns everything at 8 mana.

I considered three directions: Golgari self-mill, which keeps all three named cards; Dimir midrange, which fits Spider-Man and Bringer but drops Town Greeter; and a Dimir-plus-mill hybrid. I chose Golgari because it's the only one that keeps all three cards. It borrows the Golgari Roots shell, and the blue splash (7 sources) is for Spider-Man alone.

The honest caveat: this is slow. The win line is fully drawn by turn 8 in only about 8% of games, and the Golgari Roots shell is just 0.3% of the field, so expect it to struggle against Izzet Aggro and Vivi Cauldron. The removal suite (Bitter Triumph, Shoot the Sheriff, Villainous Wrath) is there to survive until the mill and reanimation take over.

winLine.does: Turn 2: mill four, putting creature cards in the graveyard and a land into hand.
Turn 3 impending for {1}{B}: mill four more and return Town Greeter to hand to replay for another mill four.
Turn 4 with a blue source: copy Overlord from the graveyard (its enter trigger mills four and returns a creature).
Turn 7-8 cast from hand for 8 mana: each player sacrifices other creatures, then all creature cards in both graveyards return, leaving a 6/6 flier and a board of recurred creatures.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a brew: red-green landfall with a light blue splash for Spell Snare, 24 lands and 36 spells. The plan is to ramp into Traveling Chocobo and Mightform Harmonizer, then use the extra landfall trigger to double Mightform's power twice on a land drop. Full Bore finishes the attack, and the burn (Burst Lightning, Lightning Strike) clears blockers.

I chose this over two other directions. An Izzet tempo build around Spell Snare and Full Bore would have dropped Mightform, the centerpiece. A Simic build with Mightform and Spell Snare would have left Full Bore's red pip and haste bonus mostly unused. The red-green build keeps all three cards and borrows the Landfall shell's creatures.

Caveats:
- Screaming Nemesis is banned in this Standard card pool, though the Izzet and Boros lists in the menu still run it. I left it out, so those menu lists are not fully legal as shown.
- No published list plays these three cards together, so this is untested. The full win line is drawn by turn 5 in only about 5.5% of games, so expect it to be slow and rely on the synergies arriving over several turns.
- Spell Snare only counters mana value 2 spells, and the blue splash is thin, so it may be a dead card in some games.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:
I built a Green-White airbend deck around Appa, Airbender Ascension and Bramble Familiar, using the Selesnya Offense core as the base. It's a brew, not a proven list: no tournament list runs these three together.

I considered three directions: GW airbend with the Selesnya Offense package, Simic Ouroboroid with Bramble Familiar but no Appa or airbend, and a WU Aang build. I chose GW because it's the only one where all three requested cards work. Appa and Ascension need white, and the Selesnya one-drops and Ouroboroid supply the early board and growth.

The plan: Ascension on turn 2 and cheap creatures (Llanowar Elves, Pawpatch Recruit, Bramble Familiar) feed it quest counters. Appa flashes in to airbend those permanents, and each recast from exile makes a 1/1 Ally and another counter. Ouroboroid pumps the whole board each combat, and Elspeth doubles the tokens. The win line is turn 6.

The 60 cards are 22 lands and 38 spells, and check_deck passed with no errors or warnings. Appa is one copy because it's legendary. The sideboard is 15 cards aimed at flyers, artifacts and enchantments, and go-wide creature decks.

winLine.does: Turn 2 enchantment; every creature that enters after it adds a quest counter, and at four counters it blinks one of my creatures at end step.
Turn 1 mana and a creature entry for Ascension's counters.
Flash in at 4 mana; airbends my cheap creatures and mana dorks, and each recast from exile makes a 1/1 Ally and adds a quest counter.
Each combat puts counters on every creature I control, so the Allies and recast creatures grow into a lethal board.
Doubles the Ally and Soldier tokens and removes a blocker with -3 if needed to close.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I submitted a blue-red Elemental brew. It is untested, since no published list runs these cards together, and the win line is fragile: the simulator says every card in the T5 line is drawn by that turn in only 1.4% of games.

**Plan:** Ashling on turn 2 loots for smoothing. Flamebraider on turn 3 ramps, but its mana only pays for Elemental spells, which covers the whole top end. Shinestriker on turn 4 then sets Sunderflock's discount to 6, so Sunderflock costs about 3 on turn 5. It bounces every opposing non-Elemental creature and leaves my Elementals on the board. Bounce Off, Burst Lightning, Torch the Tower and Scalding Viper clear the way early.

**Direction:** I weighed three. Rogue runs Sunderflock but spreads across five colors with few Elementals, so the discount rarely works. The Simic Ouroboroid shell runs Bounce Off, but it has no Elementals for Sunderflock. Blue-red Elementals won because Sunderflock and Ashling both need Elementals, and Izzet Aggro supplied the burn and mana base.

**Changes during submission:** Summon: Shiva was flagged as in 0% of recent Standard decks, so I swapped it for Enraged Flamecaster, which fills the thin three-drop slot. I also left out Stormchaser's Talent because the card pool lists it as banned. The 24 lands are 8 Island, 6 Mountain, 4 Spirebluff Canal, 4 Riverpyre Verge and 2 Multiversal Passage. Sunderflock runs two copies because a third would be a dead draw too often.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
Submitted as a brew (donor: the 13-list Mono-Black archetype), a 60-card mono-black deck with 24 black sources.

**Plan:** Trade removal for the opponent's threats (Heartless Act, Bitter Triumph, Murder, Archenemy's Charm), then land Bloodletter of Aclazotz on turn 4 and Doomsday Excruciator on turn 6. Bloodletter doubles the life loss on my turn, so Excruciator's 6 flying damage becomes 12, and the deck wins around turn 8. Insatiable Avarice's tutor mode finds Excruciator or Bloodletter when I need them.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. Dimir Midrange already runs Excruciator, but in two colors BBBBBB is unreliable. Rogue runs Insatiable Avarice in only two lists and has no home for Excruciator. Mono-black supports BBBBBB and BBB on curve and borrows the Mono-Black removal and creature core, so I picked it.

**Risks to know:**
- Excruciator mills both libraries to six cards, and its upkeep draw can deck me about three turns after it lands. The deck is built to close quickly, not to grind.
- The win line completes by turn 8 in only about 14% of games (tutors aren't simulated, so this understates the Avarice help).
- Excruciator and Bloodletter run three copies each, which I explained in the submission. The sideboard is built against the top of the field: Deathmark for green and white creature decks, Duress and Day of Black Sun for control and wide boards, and Leyline of the Void for Reanimator.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and whether real decks run them together.

No published list runs all three together. I'll check the field and the Rogue shell that the one-list result points to, plus pairwise overlaps.

The Rogue shell is the only archetype that has the Flail and Phoenix together, so I'll pull its latest list. I'll also pull Boros Aggro and Izzet Aggro as candidate shells.

The Rogue reference list is U/B/R, and the Boros and Izzet lists are mostly red burn and creatures. Next I'll search the card pool for the pieces a B/R build needs: removal, equipment support, and ferocious enablers for the Phoenix.

The B/R pool is deep enough for a real build. I'll confirm the B/R dual lands the Rogue list uses, then check draw odds for the Phoenix and Elf curve.

Odds for the three cards together are low on turn 4 (12.6%), so the deck needs more than one enabler. Before building, here are three directions:

- **A. B/R midrange (chosen):** Iron-Shield Elf, Flail and Phoenix at the core, with the B/R removal and dragons from the Rogue and Boros packages. Equipment on any creature makes ferocious easy.
- **B. Boros aggro:** Burst Lightning, Hired Claw, Lightning Helix. Phoenix fits, but Iron-Shield Elf and Flail don't.
- **C. Dimir midrange with a red splash:** Floodpits Drowner and Kaito. The black half works, but the Phoenix's RR needs more red than a splash gives.

Direction A is the strongest because it keeps all three requested cards in their colors and gives them the most support. Now I'll check the draft.

The check is clean: 23 lands, 16 black and 17 red sources, average mana value 2.7. Submitting the deck now.

I built a B/R midrange brew around Flamewake Phoenix, Bloodthorn Flail and Iron-Shield Elf, using Rogue's dual lands and removal. I chose this over a Boros aggro build, which would drop Iron-Shield Elf and Flail, and a Dimir build with a red splash, which is too thin on red for the Phoenix's RR. The plan: Elf on turn 2, Phoenix on turn 3, Flail on the Phoenix on turn 4, then Terror of the Peaks or Bonehoard Dracosaur. Flail gives the Phoenix power 4, which keeps ferocious on, so it can return from the graveyard for R. Ten creatures with power 4 or more enable that return, and the removal is there to protect the line.

The line is a brew, so this is not a proven list. The only published list that runs these three together is a UBR Rogue build, and this list diverges from it. The cards are exact in the pool, but turn 5 has a low chance of playing the full line: the sequence was fully drawn by turn 5 in only 0.8% of simulated games, and the draw odds for the three cards together by turn 4 were 12.6%.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a tuned Jeskai Control list with a light black splash for Inevitable Defeat. I chose this over a Rogue-based build because Jeskai Revelation and Resonating Lute live mostly in Jeskai Control, and the Jeskai shell already runs the cheap instants and sorceries that Lute's mana doubling needs.

**The plan:** Stabilise against the wide prowess, landfall and elemental boards with Lightning Helix, Get Lost, Seam Rip, No More Lies and Day of Judgment. Then turn on Resonating Lute, which doubles land mana for instants and sorceries, to cast Jeskai Revelation by turn 5–6 (bounce, 4 damage, two Monks, draw two). Inevitable Defeat handles the last blocker. Real limits: Defeat needs red, white and black on the same turn, and 5 hard black sources give only about 72% odds of seeing black by turn 7. Its three copies are a deliberate trade-off against that.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three named cards and what real decks pair them with.

None of the three has appeared in a published list. Their shared theme is Dwarves and Equipment, so I'll search the pool for those and read the field.

The field is Prowess, Lessons and Selesnya-based decks. The Dwarf and Equipment pool is deep in red and white, which matches the colors of Dáin's Company and Kíli. I'll check the Boros archetypes on the menu and a list of Boros Weapons.

Three directions are worth weighing:

1. **R/W Dwarves and Equipment.** Dáin's Company, Kíli and Dwarven Mauler all sit in these colors, and the pool has enough Dwarves and Equipment to build around. It can borrow Boros Aggro's burn and mana.
2. **R/W Equipment-artifact shell** (Boros Weapons style). It has the equipment density but no Dwarves, so Kíli and Dáin's Company do much less.
3. **Mono-R or R/x Dwarves with Dáin Ironfoot and Thorin, Mountain-king.** Fewer of the named cards fit, and the white half of Kíli and Dáin's Company goes unused.

Direction 1 fits best, so I'll build it, borrowing Boros Aggro's removal. Next I'll check the removal and the R/W payoffs.

The R/W pool has what I need: Dwarves that hit the table on turns 2 to 4, equipment that creates Dwarf or Equipment entries for Kíli, and burn that Boros Aggro already runs. Before I assemble the list, I'll confirm the dual lands and the key equipment's legality.

Both dual lands and the key equipment are legal. I'll check the 60-card list against the Boros Weapons mana base, since it runs the same dual-land suite.

The checker wants more lands than my 16, and my curve sits at 2.07 average mana value. I'll go to 17 lands and cut Stalactite Dagger to keep the count at 60. Kíli and Dáin's Company both draw cards, which covers part of the land-count warning.

The list passes with no errors. The remaining warnings are about a 17-land count against a generic recommendation; my curve is low and aggressive, with two equip-cost reducers and two draw engines, so I'm keeping 17. I'll submit it as a brew with a turn-4 line built on Mauler, Kíli, Dáin's Company and Lost Jitte.

Two cards drew notes: Chainsaw and Shock. Both have a specific job here. I'll resubmit with reasons for each rather than swapping them.

The win-line entry combined three burn spells into one name. I'll list them as separate steps.

I built a Boros (R/W) Dwarves-and-Equipment brew, and the deck is accepted. Dáin's Company, Kíli and Dwarven Mauler have no published lists in Standard, so this is my own build, not a proven one.

I considered three directions: R/W Dwarves with equipment, an equipment-heavy Boros Weapons shell with no Dwarves, and mono-red Dwarves around Dáin Ironfoot. I chose the first because it is the only one that uses all three named cards, and it borrows Boros Aggro's burn and dual lands from the menu.

The plan is to curve Mauler, Kíli, then Dáin's Company, which finds Lost Jitte and draws off Kíli. Mauler's discount makes Jitte's equip free, and burn clears blockers. The honest caveat is that the line rarely comes together by turn 4: the simulator found that only about 0.1% of games draw every card in it by then, because it does not model tutors or card draw. Treat it as a strong early-game plan, not a reliable turn-4 kill.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Sentinel of the Nameless City, Abrupt Decay and Tear Asunder.
results.text:
I built a black-green removal-midrange deck around Sentinel, Abrupt Decay and Tear Asunder. It's a brew: no published list plays these three together, and Sentinel doesn't appear in any Pioneer list from the last 400 days, so the deck is untested.

I considered three directions. Black-green won because it is the only one that casts all three cards. Selesnya would lose Abrupt Decay and most of Tear Asunder's value, and mono-green would lose both black cards. The deck runs 4 Llanowar Elves, Sentinel, Glissa, Sheoldred and Chupacabra as threats, backed by 19 removal spells: Abrupt Decay, Tear Asunder, Go for the Throat, Fatal Push, Assassin's Trophy and Infernal Grasp, plus two Thoughtseize. The mana (22 lands) and the cheap removal suite follow Jund Sacrifice, and the Pioneer checker passed it with no errors or warnings.

The win line is Llanowar Elves turn 1, Sentinel turn 3, cheap removal to clear blockers and early threats, then Sheoldred or Glissa to close by turn 6. Sheoldred's 4 mana is the bottleneck, and Glissa has very little tournament data, so treat the list as a starting point to test.

I built a mono-red Prowess deck around the three cards, using the Mono-Red Prowess shell as the base. It's labelled a brew because the three requested cards aren't in that shell. The plan is to curve out with 1–2 mana prowess creatures, clear blockers with cheap burn and Combustion Technique, and finish with Igneous Inspiration. The submitted win line is Swiftspear → Emberheart → Burst Lightning / Reckless Rage → attack → Igneous Inspiration, turn 4.

I chose mono-red over an Izzet build, which would have been the other direction: the three cards are most-played in Izzet Prowess and Rogue, but those need blue. Mono-red gets all 20 of its red sources and a low curve, so the three cards are a natural fit. The deck runs 20 lands, 17 creatures, 3 Kumano, and 20 instants and sorceries, including the three requested cards.

Two caveats:
- Combustion Technique has only Abandon Attachments as Lesson fuel in this build, so it usually deals 2–3 damage.
- Cori-Steel Cutter and Heartfire Hero appear in the menu's Izzet and Mono-Red lists, but card_info marks them as banned in Pioneer, so I left them out.

results.text:
I submitted a Grixis (blue-black with a red splash) reanimator-tempo brew. It runs 22 lands and 38 spells, and the deck passed check_deck with no errors.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three builds. An Izzet spells deck built around Phoenix and Flow State would drop Buried Alive, and a Dimir reanimator would leave Phoenix out or splash it for one card. I chose the Grixis blend because it is the only one that uses all three cards. The fetches and duals from the Izzet and Dimir lists cover the three colors, and the Reanimator shell supplies the reanimation targets.

**The plan:** Buried Alive on turn 4 puts Archon of Cruelty, Griselbrand and Arclight Phoenix into the graveyard. On turn 5, Animate Dead returns Archon, which makes the opponent sacrifice a creature, discard and lose 3. Brainstorm, Ponder and Lightning Bolt then make three instants or sorceries in one turn, so Phoenix returns with haste.

**Caveats:**

- Drawing a Buried Alive by turn 4 is about 53% on the play, and Reanimate or Animate Dead is about 68%. The full win line is drawn by turn 6 in only about 2% of games.
- Phoenix is a recurring 3-power flier, not a finisher on its own. Archon is the real threat.
- The sideboard is built to address Dimir, Izzet and Sneak and Show. It includes Force of Negation, Pyroblast, Toxic Deluge and Murktide Regent.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I submitted a 60-card Premodern brew built around Living Death, with a 15-card sideboard.

**Plan:** Fill the graveyard with fatties (Survival of the Fittest discards, Hermit Druid mill, Bone Shredder and Phyrexian Delver as extra bodies), then cast Living Death on turn 4–5 with Dark Ritual or Birds. It returns the graveyard creatures, such as Visara the Dreadful and Symbiotic Wurm, while my board creatures die. Exhume, Animate Dead and Reanimate are backup routes to the same fatties.

**Direction:** I considered three. A blue-based Reanimator shell, which is the most-played home for Living Death (42 lists) but needs blue. BG Survival, which fits Living Death's discard engine. The Hermit Druid mill package, which is the most-played Premodern combo (4.3% of the field). I chose a BG hybrid: Survival's discard engine with Reanimator's reanimation suite, because it keeps the Living Death lines and uses the BG mana base.

**Caveats:**
- Living Death also returns the opponent's graveyard creatures, and it sacrifices my own battlefield creatures without returning them. It works best when my fatties are in the graveyard and my board is empty.
- The full win line is slow. The tool estimates about 1% of games have every card in it by turn 5. Treat this as a midrange reanimator, not a turn-4 combo.
- Living Death appears in only 7 recent lists, so there is no proven list to copy. This build is my own.
